title: Bayesian Optimization for Expensive Objectives
interviewAnswer: Bayesian optimization fits a surrogate model of an expensive black-box objective and uses an acquisition function to choose promising evaluations, useful for costly hyperparameter or experiment tuning.
keyPoints: Best when evaluations are expensive, not huge-dimensional.
why: Bayesian Optimization for Expensive Objectives appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Bayesian optimization fits a surrogate model of an expensive black-box objective and uses an acquisition function to choose promising evaluations, useful for costly hyperparameter or experiment tuning. Acquisition balances exploration/exploitation. Best when evaluations are expensive, not huge-dimensional. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Tune a simulation parameter set when each experiment takes hours rather than brute-force grid search.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
